text.p: France on Monday welcomed the Nairobi summit on the crisis in central Africa's Great Lakes region while regretting the shelving of a U.N. multinational force to help the region's refugees.
A Foreign Ministry spokesman said Paris welcomed Kenya's initiative in organising the talks on the conflicts in Zaire and Burundi.
The talks were due to bring together the presidents of South Africa, Eritrea, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia and Zimbabwe and Ethiopia's prime minister. Zaire is boycotting the meeting.
"All efforts towards rapprochement and dialogue must be encouraged to facilitate an early start to preparations for the International Conference on the Great Lakes," the spokesman said.
Paris has been pushing for an international peace conference on the region's conflicts. The Nairobi summit will focus on the search for a ceasefire and political settlement in eastern Zaire.

Rebels there launched a well-planned offensive in mid-October and now control eastern key towns. They say their ultimate goal is to end the 31-year reign of Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko who is due to return to Kinshasa on Tuesday.
The spokesman said France regretted the multinational force agreed on by the United Nations would be dissolved at the end of this month.

"We believed it could have played a major role for relief to refugees and displaced people. For now, it is essential to give humanitarian organisations all the support that is necessary to allow then to continue their missions in Kivu," he said.
Plans for the force were formally shelved last weekend. About half the 1.1 million Rwandan refugees in Zaire returned home peacefully last November and the exact number remaining is disputed.
